| REG-212 | Overview | Two responsive corrections to the Lead Details info column and FILES card (user 2026-08-30), both deviations the mock cannot show because it draws one width. **FILES row**: the mock (858:24943, a 430px card) draws four slots — folder + two files + "+10" — and 858:25922 (396px, quick links expanded) draws the same four shrunk 92 → 83, so a slot is a 92px tile that may shrink to ~83, 8 apart. The card is responsive though, and a fixed three tiles left the row half empty once the info column collapsed. The two mocks are two samples of one behaviour, not two sizes — a 92px tile that shares the row and shrinks as the row tightens. `files-card.tsx` measures the row with a ResizeObserver and picks the slot count whose evenly-shared width lands closest to 92 (`TILE` 92 · `GAP` 8 · `DEFAULT_SLOTS` 4 for the first paint and wherever the width cannot be measured); the CSS then divides the row by `--slots`, so the tiles are equal and **nothing is left over on the right** (the first pass capped them at 92px and left dead space — user 2026-08-30, second round). Measured, trailing space 0 at every width: 1280 → 2 tiles + "+11" at 98 · **1440 → 4 slots at 91.5, the mock** · 1600 → 87.6 · 1920 → 5 tiles + "+8" at 98.3 · 2560 → 9 tiles + "+4" at 87.8, always inside the mocks' own 83–92 band ±. A lead with fewer files than slots keeps the tile size and leaves the row short rather than stretching one file across the card. **Detail values never truncate**: `info-column.module.css` drops `white-space: nowrap` / `text-overflow: ellipsis` from `.text` and `.contactText` for `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (rows keep a 20px min height, `.contactRow` aligns to flex-start), so a long "Property address" wraps to a second line instead of being clipped — this is the detail page, the place a value is read in full. The rule covers every **value** in the column, so the lead name (24/Bold/32) and the assignee names wrap too; their rows grew from a fixed `height` to `min-height` with `align-items: flex-start`, and the name's Edit control keeps a 6px top margin — (32 − 20) / 2 — so at rest the row is pixel-identical to the mock (verified: row 32, pencil 20 at +6). **Labels** (`.key`, `.sectionTitle`) and table / list cells keep their ellipsis: there the column width is the design | user-directed |

A 20-agent audit (10 readers + 10 adversarial skeptics, 69 candidates → 43 confirmed, 26 rejected) found the same defect class the FILES card had, across 37 files. **Rows frozen at one container width:** the Files grid and folder band (`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(299px, 1fr))` — tiles filled only at a 1244px row and orphaned the rest everywhere else); kanban columns (`flex: 1 0 320px; max-width: 480px` — shrink stays 0 so the unscoped 7-column board is untouched); the Questionnaire row (`flex: 1 1 auto` on the questions column, the 480 summary stays fixed); Settings' panel (25% of the card empty at 1440); the Quotes/Contracts grids (shrinkable floors so the row compresses together instead of being sliced by the body's `overflow: clip`). **Mock FRAME heights transcribed as element heights:** five empty-state cards (`height: 784px` → `flex: 1; min-height: 480px`, the sibling `search-empty.module.css` rule) and both Deleted sheets (`928px` → height to content) — 784 is the output of "the card fills the tab body" at the mock's 24px bottom padding, so `.centre:has([data-testid$='-empty'])` restores that padding for an empty tab and the mock's 784 comes back exactly, without the 64px of pointless scroll. **Counts frozen from sample data:** MY WORK's 2-row cap (its label printed the real total — Farah Ahmad read "Upcoming · 4" above 2 rows), kanban card avatars (measured like the FILES row), the import wizard's step-3 preview (rendered all 14 mock columns instead of the 7 mapped: 1,149px of empty grid with a populated column stranded past two blank ones), the leads PDF export's character cap (now derived from the real column pitch). **Truncation on values that must be read:** the Activity feed sentence and the file viewer's Information panel now wrap (REG-212's rule). **Menus positioned by row count → by measurement:** the Quotes / Contracts / listing row kebabs decide their side from the space actually below the trigger; the shared menu caps its height and scrolls; the Customise popover is viewport-aware. **Sample data shown as real:** the Won panel offered `Contract_OliviaM_signed.pdf` on all 36 leads (and persisted it) — now derived from the lead, still exactly that string for Olivia; the Task panel's attachment tiles show the real file's thumbnail and kind instead of the Move-stage chat screenshot + PDF glyph; a picked `.pdf` renders as a PDF in the Return wizard and the attach modal; a lead's second contract is numbered. Rejected as design intent, not defects: 26, including a proposed ResizeObserver on a column that is a fixed 191px on every viewport | audit 2026-08-30 / user-directed |
| REG-214 | Settings/Quotes | **Quote approval is a studio setting and the quote's lifecycle derives from it** (user 2026-08-30: "in this studio setup the quote required approval… now it has to be dynamic based on the studio setup"). New `quote_approval` key in `settings` (`lib/settings/types.ts`, default `required` — the studio the mocks were drawn for), a second Settings › Leads section built on the Stage movement pattern, and `quoteStatuses(approval)` / `quoteStepIndex()` in `lib/leads/quote-filters.ts`: **required** = Draft → Sent for Approval → Approved → Sent to Client → Signed; **not required** = Draft → Sent to Client → Signed. One derivation feeds all three surfaces — the Overview widget's track, the row status menu and the Filters modal — so a studio can never set a status its own widget does not show. The widget's track was the mock's fixed "Draft · Sent · Approved" (858:25057); it is now one bar per stage, each **as wide as the label beneath it and starting where that label starts** (a 2-row CSS grid over `max-content` columns, `justify-content: space-between`), labels on one line, never wrapped or broken. Iterated with the user: equal segments → wrapped "Sent for Approval"; single-line spread → labels not aligned to the notches; text-width segments → accepted. A quote holding a status the studio has since retired still reads at the furthest step it actually passed | user-directed |

| REG-217 | Shell | **Tab navigation no longer flashes its ghost** (user 2026-08-30: "every time i click a tab it loads", "why is there a jerk"). Three causes, all fixed: `PageReveal` held the skeleton for a **minimum 650ms after the page arrived**, and when the server answered before `loading.tsx` ever painted it still waited the full beat — so a fast navigation got MORE skeleton than a slow one; the hold now applies only when a ghost actually painted (`ghostClock.shownAt` non-null), which keeps the full beat on cold loads and removes it entirely on warm ones. The tab links prefetch in **full** (`prefetch` — the default fetches only the loading boundary, i.e. exactly the flash being removed), and `experimental.staleTimes.dynamic = 30` stops the router treating every `force-dynamic` entry as stale on arrival, which was re-fetching what had just been prefetched. Measured at 1440 across all seven tabs: ghost visible 373ms / 452ms on Quotes / Notes before, **0ms on every tab** after. Safe because every mutation goes through a server action that calls `revalidatePath`, which evicts those entries | user-directed |
| REG-218 | Questionnaire | Unanswered questions sort to the top of the tab; answered ones follow as a record (user 2026-08-30). A stable sort in `fetchLeadQuestions`, so each group keeps the tab's own `sortOrder` / `createdAt` sequence | user-directed |
| REG-219 | Cross | **State frozen from the mock made dynamic** (user 2026-08-30: "since we designed in Figma it will be hard coded and once we build the prototype no hardcoded things should exists"). REG-213 swept LAYOUT hard-coding; this is the other class — a mock is a picture of ONE moment (one selected item, one route, one status), and building it faithfully bakes that moment in as a constant. An 18-agent audit confirmed 23 of 39 candidates. The shape, and the case that named it: `app/leads/app-rail.tsx` listed `{ icon: 'people_alt', label: 'Leads', href: '/leads', fill: true }` — the mock was drawn on the Leads screen, so the filled glyph became a property of the ITEM and Leads read as selected on Qanvast Ops and Settings too; now `fill={active}`, a value the component already computed. **Wrong data reaching the DB:** `uploadFile` wrote the mock's single row (kind image · the floor-plan thumbnail · image/jpeg) whatever was picked, so a PDF showed correctly right up to the moment it was saved and then became a photograph — it now derives kind / mime / thumb from the name, exactly as the two client surfaces already did; the Files tab dropped the picked name entirely, persisting every upload as the action's `'Living Room'` default; `addTask` omitted `creatorId` where every other writer stamps it, so tasks added from the listing / Overview popovers and from Suggested tasks read "System created the task" and vanished from the Creators filter; `setQuoteStatus` back-filled `approvedAt` on **Signed** as well as Approved, wrong in a studio with no approval step (REG-214); the import parser accepted only the five active `STAGES` where the vocabulary is `ALL_STAGES`, silently landing an imported On Hold / Lost row in New. **A gate enforced in one place and granted in another:** Create quick links › Call Log / Meeting set the Move-stage target directly, past the page's own `requestStageChange` — on Olivia (New, linear) the header pill refuses Met with "Complete Contacted first" while the quick link opened it, and `moveStage` has no server guard, so the lead landed in Met with no Contacted log. Gated via a new `openStageLog()` that opens the window straight only for a current or completed stage (routing everything through `requestStageChange` would have made Call Log a no-op on a lead already in Contacted and lost REG-168's "add another log"). **Capabilities frozen at the mock moment:** the FILES card's tiles answered "coming soon" behind the comment "no tab designed yet" — untrue since REG-181, and the card's own "+n" tile already navigated; they now open the folder (`?folder=`) or the viewer. **A cold load showing another screen's ghost:** `[id]/loading.tsx` rendered the Overview skeleton for everything beneath it, so a hard load of a wide tab painted an info-column layout that route does not have and then handed over to a differently shaped one — the failure REG-74 exists to prevent. A new `[tab]/loading.tsx` derives the variant from the pathname (guarding `meetings`, which really is narrow); warm tab clicks are untouched (REG-217). **Bulk delete overreaching:** "Delete All" appeared when the selection covered the VISIBLE rows, so filtering to one match and pressing select-all offered to delete every task on the lead; it now compares against the lead's full list, as the toolbar's own Delete all does. Also: the Save-as-Template switches reset to true instead of reading the chosen template's stored values; the attach toast painted the mock photo beside a picked PDF; the merge preview computed "Merged result" differently from the action that merges (promising a value for three fields the merge does not write); the Quotes table always drew "Approval Date" though the component knows the studio's lifecycle; the XLSX writer named every worksheet "Leads"; the Contacted brief asserted "no questionnaire yet" as a constant beside a card counting 7 / 11 answered; the wizard dated its auto-added task from the FIRST log with a next step rather than the newest; `validateStage` required the next-step fields for one hard-coded outcome where the panel decides from `NEXT_STEP_BY_OUTCOME`; two file glyphs were `'image'` outright, reachable only once uploads could persist a PDF | audit 2026-08-30 / user-directed |

Verified: 13-case behaviour gate (every case fails on pre-fix code), search 15/15, responsive gate clean at 390/768/1440, desktop byte-identical | user-directed |
| REG-287 | Cross | **The focus trap was silently off wherever it mattered most** — found by testing, not by review, while closing REG-286's gaps. Two real bugs in the shared `components/om/surface.ts` policy: (1) `isTopmostSurface` skipped a surface's ANCESTORS but not its DESCENDANTS, and `compareDocumentPosition` reports a descendant as FOLLOWING — so any nested surface demoted its own host; (2) worse, the Tab trap deferred to `isTopmostSurface` at all. The Lead form's assignee picker portals a `role="listbox"` to `<body>` that stays mounted while focus tabs onward, so from the moment that field was reached the form switched OFF its own trap and Tab walked into the listing behind an `aria-modal` dialog. Esc still uses the topmost rule (the top layer owns Esc); the trap now asks only where focus IS — the handler's existing "focus inside another surface keeps that surface's tab order" check is the precise version. The trap also moved to the CAPTURE phase, because the DS Button is a react-aria pressable that stops keydown propagation, so a bubble listener never saw the Tab leaving the last control. Also fixed: `lead-form.tsx` never received the trap at all (my own planning error — it was moved between agent allowlists for the phone fix and lost the assignment). Verified: trapped through 25 Tabs and 15 Shift+Tabs, Escape closes, and the four hand-rolled modals in the gate still trap | bug fix |

Done as a ten-batch agent migration, each batch adversarially reviewed against the rule, then a completeness sweep over every stylesheet. Two tooltip fallbacks that show a caption because the DS Tooltip never fires on a touch pointer (the file viewer's zoom-fit label, the Lead Stages card's "why" caption on a blocked row) travel with the touch query too — the sweep flagged them as borderline and they were kept, since an iPad is exactly the case they exist for. the active row's QTY box had 15px for its digits ("6." for 681) — the QTY / UNIT / ROOM / DISCOUNT / GST cells give their 36px controls the room at p8 (the mock widens UNIT to 183 and ROOM to 159 in a frame of its own; a table cannot grow one row's cells without breaking every other row's alignment, so the columns stay put — deviation); the floating "Expand" was cut in half by the ITEM cell's overflow (the active row lifts above its neighbour); the group chevron sits 20 from the edge; the column settings' ITEM DETAILS switches saved but changed nothing — Show item description / images / autonumber now hide the description line and Expand, the thumbnail, and the # column; the panel's two lists share one 36px pitch; Issuing Entity and Add Item are the DS field at **36** (`TextField size="s"`, no raw `<input>` left); the Add Item popover opens on **typing** (spec 03), Create New Item is always live (a blank "Item" line when nothing is typed), "My Items (n)" counts what the filter shows. **Logic**: a queued 600 ms cell write is settled BEFORE any structural write reloads the lines (it used to snap back on screen and land on the server unseen), dropped for lines being removed, and forgotten whole by undo / redo (the snapshot already says what the lines should be); **a group's answer is its children's** — the chip sits on the group row and a child's STATUS cell is empty (spec 03), so the server cascades a group's status to its lines, a line joining a group takes the group's, grouping takes the lines' shared answer, and `countedLines` leaves out everything under a Declined group (a Declined group's own row sums what the client passed on) — the demo's Declined line moves to a top-level item on OM-10008 (repair R23, two new checks); undo / redo's replace validates every row first and runs delete + inserts in one transaction (REG-286); Round Prices refuses a total under S$100 ("Total is under S$100 — nothing to round") instead of discounting the quote to S$0.00, and says when it moves a % discount to S$; a unit price can no longer go negative (the markup is bounded by the cost, "−" leaves the money filter); the additional discount is stored as the value applied (% ≤ 100, S$ ≤ subtotal) and the card shows that; drag reorder stamps the quote and reloads the lines if the write fails. **React**: Escape in a cell discarded the draft on screen but `blur()` committed it (a `cancelled` ref, read live); Upload Logo toggled Show Full Content — it answers coming soon; the table carries `columnheader` / `cell` roles, the Add Item row is a row, its field a combobox (aria-expanded / controls / activedescendant, ArrowUp / Down walk the matches, Enter picks); drill-down menus move focus onto the new level's first row and the icon tiles are menu rows; every radio-style menu (status, View by, density, visibility, unit, label, discount unit) says which value is current (`DropdownItem role="menuitemradio" checked`); the thumbnail, eye, bucket fold and column handle carry the Tooltip, and ArrowUp / Down on a column's handle reorders it. **Responsive**: every Items menu is a bottom sheet at ≤767 (`PortalMenu sheetTitle`, opt-in — the Add Item combobox and TextField selects stay anchored to their field); the section toolbar is ONE row at ≤1024 (the AI mark, Create as its icon, a kebab folding Create Group · Undo · Redo · Expand · Column settings · Row density › · View by › · Collapse All — REG-354 / REG-384, via `useMediaQuery`); 20px marks take 44 boxes (−12), the drag handle and the row "+" step aside on touch (HTML5 drag never starts from a finger; Add Item › Below is the same action) so the selection cell is the checkbox alone; the cell inputs and selects stand 44 tall under a finger; ≤1024 the selection · # · ITEM block freezes on the left (ITEM narrowed to 240) with a shadow once panned; the Add Item content sticks to the left edge at any offset. **Open on the phone**: at 390 nothing is frozen (a frozen 352 beside a frozen 140 leaves no window) and the lines stay a sideways scroller — an interim; A number box takes a **sum** — "=12*3.5", "=1200/4", "=20%*300" — worked out on commit by a small recursive-descent parser (`lib/quotes/arith.ts`, never `eval`); one that does not work out leaves the value. A **sum row** under the lines totals Qty, Cost, Markup, Unit Price and Total over the lines that price (its Total is the card's subtotal); it is measured into the content-fit. **Sort by head** on Item, Qty, Cost, Markup, Unit Price and Total was built here — a press wrote the order, a second turned it round — and removed the same day (REG-483). **Find**: a search glyph in the toolbar opens a 240 box (Escape clears it) that narrows the rows to the names and descriptions carrying the text, each under its group and bucket; the sum row keeps the whole quote. Found on the way: a reload after a structural write or an undo landed a beat later and hid a value typed in that beat — every reload now merges the cell writes still queued over the stored rows, and a reload another has overtaken is dropped. Not copied from Excel: cross-cell formulas, merged cells, free extra columns. Probe `probe-excel2.cjs` (42 checks, 1440); `design-source/verify/quote-editor/items-paste-dialog.png` · `items-excel-phase3.png`. | user-directed |

| REG-569 | Quote template editor | **The second visual pass, and plainer words** (owner 2026-09-23, with a screenshot of the Details rows: "a lot of things looks broken in the quotes template editor and preview … go through the whole flow component by component and div by div across viewports and fix all the visual issues and simplify the ui … it's more sounding like technical language … too techie for a old studio owner"). A screenshot sweep of every state at 1440 · 1280 · 1025 · 768 · 390 (`tpl-sweep.cjs`, 49 shots) found: **(1) the Details rows and the Items columns had squeezed their value / heading boxes to a sliver** — a label, a value, a field button and ▲ ▼ ✕ on one 288px line. Each is now a **card on two lines**: the label (or the switch and the column's name) with its move / remove buttons, then the value with its field menu (or the printed heading, its width and alignment). **(2) The Insert field menu was clipped by the pane's edge** — it is a portal now, and every value box that carries a field says what it prints as on the quote on the page ("Prints as: Mr & Mrs Tan"), so the words in braces stop reading as code. **(3) A row added to the header's Details box printed over "Dear Sir / Mdm" and the body** — canvases lay their content out now: an element whose height comes from its words (text, details, signature, badges, page number) pushes down whatever starts inside it (a box or a picture is a background and pushes nothing), and the header or footer grows to hold everything, the body starting under its real bottom (`components/templates/render/canvas.tsx`, the document's `canvasH`). The stored positions never change — a pushed element is only drawn lower — so the print matches the editor. **(4) The Letter house style's footer printed the signature over the studio's address** (the address sat at 16 mm under a ~20 mm signature): the preset moves it to 22 mm in a 36 mm footer and repair R37 moves every stored copy of that design the same way. **(5) The top bar clipped a chip mid-word and lost the saved stamp below 1440** — the stamp sits after the chips and keeps its width, and below 1320 the chips wrap under the name. **(6) The quote preview's bar at 768 broke its template chip into three lines over the title** — the chip stays on one line and the actions take their own line up to 1024. **(7) Half-column selects and numbers truncated their words** ("Same as th…", "Label width (m…"): the font select spans the pane, the Details box's two numbers are full width. **Plainer words** (the owner's worry, and the design lead's call: the editor is for a studio owner, not a layout engine): the left tabs are **Page · Brand · New quotes** (were Structure · Brand · Defaults); "Add block" is **Add to the page**; blocks read *Picture · Line across · Blank space · New page* (were Image · Divider · Spacer · Page break); a canvas lists what is *on the header* and offers *Add to the header*; the element head reads "Details in the header" (was "Details · Header"); Rule → Line, weight → thickness, "Keep with the next block" → "Keep together with what follows", "Group by / Then by" → "Group the items by / Then split each by", "Section bands" → "Section headings", "Header row" → "Column headings", "Zebra rows" → "Shade every other row", "Zero amounts" → "A line that costs nothing prints", "Mark" → "Above the line", "Type" → "Fonts" (the Brand tab and the kit page), "Right block" → "On the right", "Value lines: None / Underlined (form)" → a switch "Underline the values, like a form", "Page setup · A4 · 12/18/10/18 mm" → "Page setup · A4". Probes `verify-tpl-audit.cjs` (9) + `verify-template-editor.cjs` (28) rerun on the renamed words; screenshots in `design-source/verify/template-editor/pass-2/`. Later the same day: the preview's template chip, made `nowrap` here, overflowed a 320 phone by 57px under a long template name — it caps at the row's width and its name ellipsizes (the 320 gate of `verify-round1-responsive.cjs`). | user-directed |
| REG-570 | Quote editor | **The Items section's heads hold while the table scrolls, and the sideways scrollbar stays in reach** (owner 2026-09-23: "while scrolling the item header can be sticky until it reaches the end of the container so that the item and table headers are visible in the viewport"; the Items-table UX audit, `design-source/context/quote-editor/03-items-table-ux-audit-2026-09-23.md` A1 · A2, built on the owner's "go ahead"). Measured before: after 700px of scroll the section top sat at −51 and the column heads at 17, both gone under the tab strip; the sideways scrollbar sat 1,924px below the heads. Cause: the head row lived inside the sideways scroller, and CSS sticky only holds to the nearest scrolling ancestor. Built: the section card's top holds (`SectionCard sticky`) at `--editor-sticky` (header 76 + tab strip 48 = 124; 48 at ≤767, where the header leaves the stack), and the column heads live in a bar of their own above the scroller (`.headBar`, sticky at 124 + the top's measured height — `--section-top-h` from a ResizeObserver, so a wrapping toolbar at 1025–1199 still lines up), scrolled sideways in step with the body (each follows the other's scrollLeft; the echo of a value one side set is recognised and dropped — it used to write a stale offset back into a body mid-way through a smooth pan and stop it); the frozen ITEM / TOTAL heads keep their places because the bar is a scroller too. Both let go when the card's end passes (sticky's own rule; measured: the top's bottom stays inside the card). A held head casts the 1px rule and a soft shadow (`useStuck`, `components/om/use-stuck.ts`, listening to every scroller on the page). In the full-page Expand the card's body is the scroller and the heads hold at its top. The native scrollbar is hidden; a 24px bar sticks to the viewport's bottom while the table runs on — a pager at each end, a track whose thumb is the visible share (drag the thumb, press the track, press a pager; the pagers hide under a finger) — and rests at the table's foot once the end is on screen; not drawn while the table fits. Verified: `verify-items-ux.cjs` (47) at 1440 / 768 touch / 390 touch; screenshots `design-source/verify/items-ux/`. | user-directed |
| REG-571 | Quote editor | **Rows drag with the pointer, like the Payment Schedule, and a line can be dropped into another section** (owner 2026-09-23: "drag and drop vertically and horizontally is not visually smooth transition like it is in the payments"; audit B1 · B3 — dropping into a section was the owner's yes on the audit's first question). Before: the browser's own HTML5 drag from the 20px handle — the ghost was the handle icon, a 2px line marked the slot, nothing slid, the row jumped into place after the server wrote, and a drop beside another parent was refused with a snackbar. Built (`components/quotes/editor/items/row-drag.ts`): the pressed row lifts (elevation 3) and follows the pointer — a section with everything under it as one block — riding a CSS variable (`--row-dy`), so no move re-renders a row; the rows it passes slide by its height (160ms); the slot follows the row under the pointer: its upper half = before it, its lower half = after it among ITS siblings, under an open section's title = first inside it, past the last row = the end of the table; the lifted row's ITEM cell indents to the slot's depth (flush · 32 · 56), so the eye knows where the line will land before it is let go; on release the block settles into its gap (170ms) and the order lands in the same render, never jumping back first. The lines move at once; the parent change (`setQuoteItemParent`) and the sibling order (`reorderQuoteItems`) are written after, a failed write reloads; "Moved into “Bedrooms”" / "Moved out of the section" when the parent changed; the dropped row pulses (REG-573). Refused slots keep the last good one: inside itself, a section into a sub-section, a section that holds sub-sections anywhere but the top (REG-558), a line into another View-by bucket. The window (or the Expand's scroller) scrolls while the pointer rides its edge; Escape cancels; the block never leaves the table's own height (the ghost stops at the first and last row, so the sideways scroller never grows a vertical bar). A finger drags too: the handle is back on touch (REG-273 had hidden it because HTML5 drag never starts from a finger), with a 32×44 box, the selection cell 80 (handle · checkbox); the page wears the grab cursor and nothing selects while a drag runs (`html.om-row-dragging`). Move to section stays in the row menu. Found on the tablet screenshot and fixed here: the row numbers walked the siblings in ARRAY order, so an optimistic reorder showed "5" above "4" until the next reload — `numberItems` orders by position now (lib/quotes/math.ts) and the drop keeps the array in position order. Probe: `verify-items-ux.cjs` — lift · slide · settle · written · into a section · Escape · a finger at 768. | user-directed |
| REG-572 | Quote editor | **A dragged column's body cells travel with its head** (owner 2026-09-23; audit B2). REG-462's head drag slid the heads while the body's cells swapped only on release. The column-drag hook writes the dragged head's offset to `--col-dx` on the table's `[data-drag-root]`, and `style(key)` now goes on every body cell of that column (rows, the sum row, the view buckets), so the whole column follows the pointer and the passed columns slide with their heads; the offset rides the variable, so a move never re-renders a row and React hears only when the head passes a neighbour. Every other table keeps its head-only drag, unchanged. | user-directed |
| REG-573 | Quote editor | **Every row that just arrived is brought into view and pulses; a new section takes the caret** (owner 2026-09-23: "when i add a new section it adds at the bottom and there is no auto scroll to the bottom"; audit C1 · C2). Measured before: a new section landed 2,529px down, out of view, the focus left on the toolbar button, the snackbar the only feedback. Built (`attention`, items-section.tsx): two frames after the reload the row is centred when it sits under the sticky heads or off the screen (`scrollIntoView` centre, the Expand's scroller too), pulses once (`data-fresh`, a 1.4s primary wash at 14%), and — New section from the toolbar, Create ▾ and the bulk bar, "Section with n items", a new line from Create ▾ / the leading + / the edge + / Add item above · below / a blank Add Item entry — its name holds the caret with the words selected, so typing replaces "New section" or "Item". | REG-577 | Quote templates | **A template just published no longer reads "Unpublished changes", and edits after a publish read as one story** (owner 2026-09-23, a card reading "Unpublished changes" over "Published v1 · just now by Dane": "unpublished and published it has both the status"). Two things were wrong. **A false draft**: Publish clears the draft on the server, but the editor's autosave timer (900ms after the last edit) races the flush Publish does and could land a draft write after the publish — a draft equal to what had just been published, which the card read as "Unpublished changes" off `draft_json` alone; and the line's "just now" was the draft's stamp, not the publish's. `saveTemplateDraft` now stores no draft when the design and defaults equal the published ones (canonicalised through the parsers), and the gallery's `hasDraft` compares the draft with the published design + defaults, so a stale row reads right too. **The words**: a real draft over a published version no longer says "Published" and "Unpublished" on one card — the ribbon reads **Edited since v1**, the line "Published v1 · 3 days ago · edited just now by Dane" (the publish's stamp first, then the edit's), the table's status note "edited since v1", the editor's chip "Edited since v1", its kebab "Discard the edits since v1" and the confirm "Discard the edits since v1? … The edits since are lost." Verified by `verify-template-status.cjs` (an identical draft written by hand, a differing one, and the editor's own edit → publish → edit → undo path) and the editor suite rerun. | bug fix · user-directed |

| REG-708 | Every page's ghost is its own page, and the loader and the reveal draw the same one | Owner 2026-09-28: "a lot of new pages added to company or other pages the ghost loading is different from the page content and the loader. Filmed on the production build, a full load of a lead's Files tab painted the **Leads listing's** ghost, then a table ghost, then the file grid; Company pages painted Templates' tab strip over four blank cards, then two tall bones, then the page. **Two causes, two fixes.** (1) A parent's `loading.tsx` wraps its children and paints first on a full load, so each loader now wraps its own page only — the parent pages moved into route groups, the URLs unchanged: `app/leads/(list)` · `app/leads/[id]/(overview)` · `app/quote-x-ray/(home)` · `app/company/plan/(usage)` · `app/company/price-book/(items)` · `app/company/templates/(libraries)` (the five galleries share one ghost; Brand kit has its own) · `app/(editor)/quotes/[quoteId]/(edit)` · `app/(editor)/contracts/[id]/(edit)` · `app/sign/[id]/(sign)`; `app/company/loading.tsx` is gone (Company's index is a redirect). (2) **One ghost per page, drawn by both its `loading.tsx` and its `PageReveal`** — never a count or a variant only the page knows, so the hand-over between the two is invisible — built from the **ghost kit** (`components/shell/ghost-kit.tsx`: the L1 / L2 headers, the tab strip, `Line`, `Slot` — a control's box whose size follows the control's own rules per width and pointer: the 48 field, 36 → 44 selects, the search folding into its glyph at ≤1024, New ▾ folding on a phone — `GhostField`, `GhostTable` with its Add row and its phone cards, and **`Words`**: the page's own sentence in its own class with the letters hidden and each line drawn as a bar, so a help text wraps in the ghost exactly as on the page) on the page's own layout classes. New ghosts: Company › Profile · Members · Questionnaire · Integrations · Plan & AI credits › Usage · Plan & billing · Brand kit · the template galleries · Price book › My Items · My Sections (`components/company/company-ghosts.tsx`, the frame `company-ghost-frame.tsx` draws the L2 header when opened with `?from=`); Materials and the AI Visualizer's home draw the usual page in both (their reveal counted the studio's cards); Leads › Insights (`insights-ghost.tsx`); the rail's Tasks, Tools › Quotes, Tools › Contracts (`components/shell/list-ghosts.tsx`, on the lead tabs' toolbars and tables with the studio columns); **each lead tab's own body** (`components/leads/detail/tab-ghosts.tsx` — the Tasks, Quotes and Contracts tables at their tracks and row heights, Files' folders and tiles, Notes' list and pane with the phone's composer, the question cards beside the summary, the Activity feed; `[tab]/loading.tsx` reads the tab from the address, `DetailTabSkeleton`), the lead strip's eight tab bones (it drew nine since Meetings hid, REG-552), the phone's lead header (the kebab on the title line) and its identity block; Settings per module (`app/settings/settings-ghost.tsx`, `?section=`); the listing by its view (`components/leads/listing-ghost.tsx`: `?view=` or the remembered view — a kanban load streamed the table's ghost, REG-197's gap) at fixed row and card counts (it streamed 8 rows and grew to 12 on hydration); X-Ray's setup scoped and with the intro as the member left it (`xray-setup-ghost.tsx`); the Tasks · T&Cs & Notes · Payments template editors (`library-editor-ghost.tsx`, they drew the quote editor's); the contract editors' Outline pane and meta row; the editors' shared header (`components/shell/editor-head-ghost.tsx`); Preview's bar on its own classes and its A4 at the document's 794; new loaders for the quote a signing link shows and the confirmation link (a blank page before). `PageReveal`'s ghost keeps its own height, as in `loading.tsx`'s flow (stretched to the page's, a column page squeezed its rows and the reveal stopped matching the loader). Verified by capture — the loader (scripts removed), the held reveal and the page, with the ghost laid over the page — at 1440 and 390 touch for 51 routes, and by filming full loads and in-app hops. | user-directed · bug fix |

| REG-711 | Keyboard shortcuts: one list, one layer, one guard | Owner 2026-09-28: "the shortcut keys looks good to me. Go ahead and build it all" — the proposal https://claude.ai/artifact/7XFQkqgqwTQujwNRNuqAkh, every question as recommended (Q-26 actions in search: later; Q-27 remapping: no). `lib/keys/registry.ts` declares every key once (id · keys · words · where; `GO`, `MARKED`, `FORMAT_KEYS`, the editors' own lists), `lib/keys/spec.ts` turns a spec into a Mac or Windows keyboard's words, `aria-keyshortcuts` and the WCAG 2.1.4 test, `lib/keys/store.ts` keeps the per-browser state (`om.keys.*`: the two switches, the keys used, the mouse counts, the tip day) and the handlers pages register (`useShortcut`, `useShortcutsHere`). `components/shell/shortcuts/shortcuts-layer.tsx` — mounted by `AppShell` and the editors' layout, never on the client's pages — is the one keyboard: letters listen first (a focused DS button can swallow a key), keys a component may answer itself (⌘Z, arrows, ↵, ⌫, Esc) listen last and stand down; never while typing or composing (IME); an open modal or menu owns the keys; a widget marked `data-kb-own` (the Items table) keeps its own. A key presses the page's own control (`data-kb="<id>"`), so it does what the press does, with the same checks and refusals; lists and tab rows are marked (`data-kb-list` · `data-kb-row` · `data-kb-open` · `data-kb-select`, `data-kb-tabs`). The ? panel (`shortcuts-panel.tsx`, the house non-modal Drawer at 360) lists only what the page in front of you answers, then Everywhere and Dialogs and menus; All pages lists every key; from 1280 the shell's pages make room for it (an editor keeps its own layout — its header is dense — and the panel lies over its right side; a control it covers wears no badge). | user-directed · invented UI (the proposal page, no mock) |

| REG-726 | The design checks: the house rules as code | Owner 2026-09-29: "i don't this to happen in the future. How can we avoid all the inconsistency for the future developments? … when the team take this repo and integrate it breaks." Every drift the audit found was a copy, and nothing failed when a rule was broken. `npm run design:lint` (`scripts/design-lint.mjs`) reads the code against eight rules — a modal draws the house head and foot · a close is the house one · colours, type and radii from the tokens · no design values in inline styles · the DS through `@/components/ds` · no copied table stylesheets — per file, against `design-lint.baseline.json`, which holds today's violations and may only go down (a new one fails with the file, the line and the house piece to use). `npm run design:anatomy` (`scripts/design-anatomy.mjs`) measures the running app: every page's table heads against the leads listing's and every dialog the pages open (C / F, REG-711) against the house head and foot, at 1440 and 390. CI runs both on every push and pull request; the PR template, `CONTRIBUTING.md` §5–7 (a new *Integrating 1.0 without breaking the design*) and `AGENTS.md` name them. CODEOWNERS already names both of the owner's accounts; branch protection on `main` (a pull request, the CI check, review from Code Owners) is his to switch on. | user-directed |

Lists inside Settings / Company cards are the one card table (components/om/card-table.module.css, `data-card-table`). After: 0 frames late, 0 rows left tinted, 0 frames split. Menus and pickers keep their fade. The design lint gains `row-fade` (`scripts/design-lint.mjs`): a background transition on a `.row` / `.cell` / `.pin` in any table stylesheet fails CI. | REG-1773 | Data · the local database | **No write collision leaves the server holding the database's lock** — the bug S08's builder found, fixed at its root (`lib/db/local-file.ts`, used by `lib/db/index.ts`). Cause, reproduced: libsql opens every connection with **no busy timeout**, so a statement that meets another process's lock (a probe's `sqlite3`, `npm run db:repair` while a server runs) fails at once with SQLITE_BUSY; and @libsql/client runs each statement through `prepare().run()` while libsql-js **never resets a statement that failed** — the half-run statement stays active until the garbage collector happens to finalize it. SQLite then stops auto-committing every later write on that connection (they keep the write lock and stay invisible to other processes — a page's "seen" stamp after a collision never landed), or, after a COMMIT that failed and its ROLLBACK, keeps a SHARED lock on the transaction's own connection — on an idle server, until it restarts. The cure: **every connection waits up to 5 s for a lock** (`BUSY_WAIT_MS`, the client's `timeout`, also given to `scripts/migrate.ts` · `repair-demo-data.ts` · `snapshot-baseline.ts`); **a transaction ends through exec** (`EndsCleanly`: COMMIT / ROLLBACK through `executeMultiple`, which finalizes its statement even when it fails; a rollback after SQLite already ended the transaction is a no-op, so the first error is the one reported); **a statement on the main connection that still fails on a lock replaces that connection** (`reconnect`) before the error goes on; **`batch` runs on its own write transaction** ended the same way. A remote libSQL database is returned untouched. The harness (now the probe's section 7): before, 6 of 12 checks failed — an autocommit write and a page's transaction refused at once, the next writes never landing, a sqlite3 write locked out; after, a short lock is simply waited for (≈1.2 s), a lock held past 5 s fails that one write cleanly, and the file is free after every case. | bug fix |

Idempotent (once the month holds today, nothing moves). Two checks: the demo's month has ended (the first page would roll it); a credits ledger row dated after now. No migration (no schema change); no new table. | user-directed |

A **run** is cells selected down one column: **Shift+click** a cell of the column the focus is in, or **Shift+↓ / Shift+↑** from a box (Excel's two ways; Shift+↓ walked the column before — on a fillable cell it now grows the run, on the Item column it still walks). The run wears the selected tint (`--om-color-primary-variant`) and a 1px primary hairline; its corner square (REG-477's fill handle) sits on its **last** cell, the focused box's own square stepping back. Dragging that square continues the run: **numbers go on by their step** (1, 2 → 3, 4; the average step for a longer run; the run's own decimals), **above the run back the other way** (1, 2 → 0, −1); **words and empty cells repeat in turn** (Living, Kitchen → Living, Kitchen …). Each column keeps its own unit and bounds (money in cents, a mark-up never below −cost, a price never below 0, Discount and GST 0–100, a quantity ≥ 0 except a variation order's omission); the studio's rounding step applies as for any edit (REG-584). **One cell still copies** (REG-477 unchanged). **⌘D over a run** fills its first cell into the rest (Excel's Ctrl+D). A press elsewhere, any other key or the focus leaving the table lets the run go; a fill lets it go too. One snapshot → **one ⌘Z** takes a whole fill back. The phone's cards are untouched (no run there); a touch tablet keeps the one-cell copy. The snackbar says the step: *"{n} cells filled — counting up by {step}"* / *"— counting down by {step}"* (money as money, a percentage with %); a repeat or a copy keeps *"{n} cells filled"*. The ? panel's Items rows gain **Shift ↓ · Shift ↑ — "Select cells down · up"** (`grid.run`, `lib/keys/registry.ts`; one line, as its neighbours). Pure rule `lib/quotes/fill-series.ts` (`seriesFill`); the table's run (`items-table.tsx`), the section's `fillDown(…, series)` (`items-section.tsx`), the cell marks `data-run` · `data-run-end` (`item-row.tsx`). ## The calm UI build (2026-10-27 → 28)

The UI audit of 2026-10-27 (18 themes, 289 findings, 650 word rows — review page https://claude.ai/artifact/NEw4ESHdVR2GmCwk2dPTKQ, record `design-source/context/ui-audit-2026-10-27/`), built as recommended as a visual, wording and UX pass that keeps every feature. Six lanes, B1–B6; staged ids → numbers in `build/reg-map.json`; what moved, for the developers, in `build/changes-for-developers.md`.
